article: Win32API and C++ for Windows application development
scope: Read the complete Japanese article and all twelve translations; compared every section, suitability list, qualitative summary, terminology, metadata, link, and asset. Checked technical claims against current Microsoft Learn documentation.
findings: Removed duplicate future dates from all editions, preserved the original publication date (2025-07-12), and set lastmod to the review date.
Replaced categorical speed and memory claims with implementation-dependent guidance.
Corrected the claim that native Win32 means a C++ app has no runtime or can always ship as a single executable; deployment depends on CRT linkage and other dependencies.
Clarified that modern DPI and accessibility support is possible but requires implementation and testing in raw Win32; global hooks can hurt performance and conflict with apps.
Clarified that C++ is portable while code calling Win32-specific APIs needs adaptation; driver development is separate and uses WDK tooling.
Replaced misleading static rating table with a qualitative summary and added Microsoft references in all editions.
